title: Million Token Cost Bridge — Regional Slab and Instance Mix
file_description: A compact spreadsheet-style model that maps GPU-instance cost and throughput into $/1M tokens by region and workload profile. Includes interactive vs batch profiles, preemptible adjustments, and simple sensitivity knobs for quantization and batching improvements.
summary: This sheet is a decision-facing calculator to compare regional unit economics (USD per 1M tokens) across instance classes and workload profiles. It intentionally uses conservative throughput assumptions and exposes a few levers (batch size, quantization uplift, preemptible discount) to show where runway or routing policies buy the most savings.
assumptions: Throughput expressed as GPU-hours required per 1M tokens (lower is better).
Interactive profile: seq_len=512, avg_out_tokens=128, batch=1, latency-optimized kernel paths.
Batch profile: seq_len=2048, avg_out_tokens=256, batch=16, sustained throughput kernels active.
Preemptible discount assumed = 30% of raw GPU-hour cost; we apply a reliability penalty (requeue / orchestration) of +0.05 USD per 1M tokens when using preemptible instances.
Quantization/optimizations: conservative savings set at 15% reduction in GPU-hours for recommended models (can be toggled).
GPU-hour list prices are indicative cloud-on-demand equivalents and include an ops markup where appropriate for reserved capacity comparators.

calculation_examples: Example row calculation: Base_cost_per_1M_USD = GPU_hrs_per_1M_tokens * GPU_hour_cost_USD
key_metrics: Typical interactive net cost range across regions: $0.84 - $1.60 per 1M tokens
Batch-optimized net cost floor: $0.13 - $0.36 per 1M tokens (with high batching and reserved capacity)
Quantization / kernel improvements can shift GPU_hrs_per_1M_tokens by ~15% (proportional impact on cost)
sensitivity_notes: If GPU-hour pricing changes +/- 20%, Net_cost_per_1M moves roughly +/-20% (linear with hour price).
If batching increases effective throughput (halves GPU_hrs_per_1M), net cost halves; this is the single biggest lever for unit economics.
Preemptible strategy: yields 20-30% gross savings but operational fallbacks/latency tail risks need to be modeled per-product.
recommended_actions: Expose a per-route routing policy that prefers batch-optimized regions for non-interactive workloads (nightly jobs, bulk embeddings).
Pilot aggressive quantization on safe model families (7B/13B) in us-east1 with A100 reserved to validate 15% GPU-hour savings assumption.
Track a weekly rolling metric in Console linking actual tokens served by model+route to realized $/1M (to close the loop on these assumptions).
Consider a small reserved commitment in eu-west1 and us-central1 to shave 8–12% off listed GPU-hour costs where steady batch demand exists.
open_questions: What is the true end-to-end failure cost (in USD per 1M tokens) when a preemptible job is interrupted and retried in our stack?
How much throughput improvement do our custom kernel patches deliver for sequence lengths >1024 in practice?
Should we include network egress and storage mount costs into the per-1M calculation for multi-region routing decisions?
